answer: Policies are written in delta, settled in grove, and pulse lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 43% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 368 aliases cost 161 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
